methodological_rigor.justification: This retrospective multicenter cohort (n=509 across six Austrian centers) uses an appropriate IPTW propensity score framework with multiple imputation (25 datasets, chained equations) to handle missing covariates, and achieves adequate balance (SMD <0.2) as reported in Supplementary Table S3. The authors appropriately address proportional hazards violations identified by Schoenfeld tests (PFS P=0.002; OS P=0.025) through flexible parametric spline models and RMST analyses, and perform a sensitivity analysis censoring at next-line therapy to address treatment crossover (yielding IPTW HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.41-1.07). Weaknesses include the absence of a prospective power/sample-size justification, non-central radiology review with heterogeneous restaging intervals (acknowledged), substantial missingness for PIK3CA/TP53/BRAFV600E (66-72%) which weakens molecular subgroup inferences, and inability to report systematic adverse events. Residual confounding remains possible, and interaction testing is explicitly exploratory.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is an individual retrospective multicenter cohort with IPTW adjustment, which maps to Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is high: the question (comparative effectiveness of three established late-line regimens in biomarker-unselected pretreated mCRC) is directly actionable, endpoints are patient-relevant (PFS, OS, DCR), and findings corroborate the SUNLIGHT RCT in a less-selected real-world population including ECOG ≥2 and earlier-line uses. The molecular subgroup findings (consistent benefit across KRAS/KRASG12; signal of lack of benefit in BRAFV600E with interaction P=0.020) have translational implications for patient selection, though BRAFV600E subgroup is small.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE applies as this is an observational multicenter cohort study. Reporting is thorough: eligibility, index date, outcome definitions (RECIST v1.1 analog), covariates, missing-data handling, propensity score derivation, balance diagnostics, and sensitivity analyses are all described, and ethics approval with IRB number is provided. Missing-data proportions are explicitly tabulated in Table 1. However, there is no mention of prospective protocol registration, no participant flow diagram, and journal-specific data/code availability sections are redacted ([REDACTED] placeholders throughout); no repository or code sharing is apparent from the retained text, limiting reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is primarily empirical: a sizeable multicenter real-world propensity-weighted comparison of three late-line mCRC regimens including the newer FTD-TPI+bevacizumab combination established by SUNLIGHT, with molecular subgroup granularity (particularly KRASG12 at 30.5% prevalence and BRAFV600E signal). Direct comparators exist — notably the Japanese administrative database propensity study by Kagawa et al. (ref 30) with similar comparative design, and the Doleschal et al. real-world KRASG12 analysis (ref 22) — which the authors appropriately cite, limiting the novelty claim. The methodological sophistication (flexible parametric time-varying models, RMST, crossover-censored sensitivity analysis) and the TP53/BRAFV600E exploratory signals are the more distinctive contributions, but overall this is a meaningful incremental extension rather than a paradigm shift.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a focused introduction that clearly articulates the three study aims, methods that are dense but systematic, and a discussion that balances positive findings with explicit limitations (central radiology, crossover, residual confounding, lack of toxicity data). The abstract is quantitatively grounded (HRs, 95% CIs, RMST differences with P values) and accurately reflects the main results. Acronyms are generally defined on first use and figure captions are informative, though Table 1 is extremely dense and would benefit from reformatting, and references to multiple supplementary figures/tables (S1-S7) with [REDACTED] links occasionally interrupt flow. Prose is clear and publication-ready with only minor repetition between discussion and results.

key_strengths: Large multicenter real-world cohort (n=509) with meaningful external validity relative to SUNLIGHT, including ECOG ≥2 and earlier-line patients
Rigorous causal inference workflow: IPTW with multiple imputation, documented covariate balance (SMD <0.2), and crossover-adjusted sensitivity analysis
Appropriate handling of PH assumption violations via flexible parametric spline models and 24-month RMST (OS gain 1.5 months, P=0.003)
Clinically relevant molecular subgroup analysis including KRASG12 (30.5% prevalence) and a BRAFV600E interaction signal (P=0.020)
Transparent reporting of limitations (no central review, no systematic AE capture, residual confounding, treatment crossover)
key_concerns: No prospective protocol registration or formal power/sample-size justification
High missingness for PIK3CA (66.6%), TP53 (71.9%), and BRAFV600E (17.3%) materially weakens molecular subgroup inferences
Non-central radiology review and non-standardized restaging intervals risk differential outcome ascertainment
Novelty is incremental — a prior Japanese administrative database propensity analysis (Kagawa et al.) reports a conceptually similar comparison
Data/code availability not evident from retained text; no safety or quality-of-life data captured
Subgroup interaction tests are explicitly exploratory with small strata (e.g., BRAFV600E n=22)
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid, clinically relevant real-world comparative-effectiveness study that corroborates and extends SUNLIGHT with meaningful molecular subgroup analyses, but with incremental novelty relative to existing real-world propensity studies — appropriate for a mid-tier oncology journal (tier 2) with minor revisions addressing missing-data impact on subgroups and data-availability specifics.
